note: The camera-focal calibration sweep. It evaluates 26 coarse candidates and 20 fine ones, each a fresh 300-iteration solve, and exports one integer focal. That focal configures the mesh renderer and feeds every FLAME landmark projection, so it determines the whole 3D tracking geometry. Every read below is the SAME clip at the SAME seed; the only variable is which code path ran and that it ran twice. The value was unobservable until this work added one print statement: not one line of that module's logging reaches any run log.

timing.note: Wall clock of the batching change, measured separately across three clips.
timing.variantNote: IMPORTANT: this timing is for the UNCONFIRMED batched sweep -- the sweep batched outright, which is the variant that was measured. The implementation that was merged instead hands the top-ranked candidates back to the untouched sequential solver for confirmation (FOCAL_BATCH_CONFIRM, default 4), because no batched Adam formulation is bit-identical to the sequential one. That trades a 9.3x iteration reduction for 3.7x, so the DEFAULT configuration should land materially below the figure here. Treat -9.61% as the ceiling, not the shipped number.

pinned.note: Two runs with the focal pinned to a constant, to test whether the unstable selection explains the pipeline's non-reproducibility. It does not: the pinned pair sits inside the unpinned identical-config population on every statistic. Wall clock is a side effect -- pinning skips the search entirely.
